identity: Ezcurrite G/1957 is grandfathered, not IMA 1957 approval. The record omits unsupported external IDs.
Rivadavite A/1966-010 is the species approval ; 1967 is publication year. The modern OH/water partition and historical oxide-water formula have identical total elemental inventories.
Natural minerals remain distinct from associated borax/kernite, elementalB, synthetic salts and traded borates. No criticality designation was searched or asserted for the species.
ezcurrite: 1967 chemistry includes possible rivadavite; no purity fraction is transferred to DTA or1973 fragment. Table 5 text column3 versus table column1 error is preserved.

1967 DTA at 20°C/min has280°C amorphization, 680°C crystallization, 780°C fusion; 575°C OH-loss assignment tentative in results despite stronger abstract. Heating versus slow-cooled products differ; no measured product composition or yield. Atmosphere/mass/replicates unspecified.

Synthesis p1058 gives two actual qualitative trials:10 g borax + 2.16 g boric acid + 10 g water boiling then 10 mL cold water and filtration; second NaCl-saturated trial above 51°C gives better crop, not numerical yield. Reagent hydration/purity, residence times and trial-specific phase analysis unavailable.

1973 crystal uses prior cell/chemistry,1974 independent reflections of which 893 were unobserved; five of seven H positions located. External factorTable 2 not acquired. Thermal anisotropy is not a heating experiment.
rivadavite: Original 1967Table 2 b=0.010versus8.010 in the abstract; no cell reconstruction adopted. The apparent218/278 DTA discrepancy is OCR-only, rejected by original scan.
DTA at 20°C/min at 218/632/797°C and 672°C exotherm; assignments to water/OH are interpretations, not gas measurements. Product remains chemically unidentified.
Separate 110°C/24 h and 300°C/30 min holds yield 45%/90% of water inventory, not bulk mass orB recovery. Table 4H2O-minus uses 95°C/24 h and must not be conflated.
Publisher/Crossref 1973volume 60versus IMA 69 preserved; metadata-only access does not validate an atomic model.
